name: Kaomoji Terminal
summary: Pulse is just a kaomoji in a terminal — (-_-) → (•_•) → (°o°;) → (^_^)b — and the human answers the roll-back prompt with one key.
look: Dark terminal with faint scanlines, JetBrains Mono everywhere, teal prompts, coral anomaly row, and one enormous kaomoji face per frame as the character.

components.name: Kaomoji face
components.role: Pulse’s entire body: 4 expressions built from ASCII

components.name: Log stream
components.role: timestamped metric lines in mono; ok in green

components.name: Hot line
components.role: the anomaly row: coral bar, tinted background

components.name: Prompt box
components.role: the question + [R] roll back / [A] acknowledge keys

components.name: Human input
components.role: ‘you> R’ with a blinking block cursor

motion.name: Type-on
motion.how: characters at 20 chars/s, 1 line per 8th note in logs; punctuation pauses snap to the next beat (120 BPM grid)

motion.name: Face swap
motion.how: hard cut between kaomoji on quarter notes, with a 1-frame scale 1.08 pop — never tweened

motion.name: Cursor blink
motion.how: block cursor 0.25 s on / 0.25 s off (8ths), holding solid while the human types

story: Hook: a log of 38 opened dashboards and a sleeping (-_-) under '> how many dashboards did you check today?'. Reveal: the screen clears to a giant (•_•), '$ acme pulse --watch all' and the Acme Pulse lockup. Proof: the stream flags 'checkout conversion −18%' at 09:42 after deploy #2231, the face gasps (°o°;), and the human types R to roll back. CTA: (^_^)b, 'resolved in 6 min', 'Every metric. Every minute.' and [ Start free ].
adapt: Replace the log lines with your own CLI or event stream, pick 4 kaomoji for your idle/watching/alert/done states, and turn your primary action into a single-key prompt.

references.note: Japanese text faces read upright, emphasising the eyes
the 1982 origin of text faces in plain-text messaging

fit.risk: Terminal aesthetics exclude non-technical buyers and dense logs are hard to read at feed size; keep only 5 log lines and one giant face per frame.
